durga-puja.headline: Kolkata: choose a neighbourhood, then explore on foot

places.name: Kolkata pandals
places.detail: Choose one compact group of neighbourhood pandals per outing for art, idols and community worship. A cross-city checklist leaves less time for the celebrations.

timeline.detail: The main five-day celebration begins; use this stage to explore the pandals you most want to see.
Rituals, worship and pandal visits continue. Confirm the timing of prayers or cultural programmes with each organiser.
Farewell and immersion mark the closing stage. View from a designated public area rather than following an immersion group to the water.

durga-puja.transport: Use the city rail or Metro network for the main journey where it fits your route, then confirm the permitted walking approach. Check festival service notices and arrange a meeting point away from the pandal entrance.
durga-puja.family: For children, choose a short daytime outing and one or two pandals, with a meal and toilet break planned. A quieter visit is a planning preference, not a guarantee about crowd levels.
durga-puja.accessibility: Ask each pandal about ramps, queue length, seating and the distance from the nearest permitted drop-off. A step-free station does not establish that the final approach or pandal is accessible.

suggestedPlan.detail: Explore one neighbourhood and leave time to look at the artwork.
Choose a different cluster or an advertised cultural programme; keep the return journey flexible.

tips: Ask before joining a ritual or photographing worshippers.
Check whether a bhog meal requires a token or advance arrangement.

onam.headline: Thiruvananthapuram for public programmes; Kochi for a different local expression

places.name: Thiruvananthapuram
places.detail: Kerala Tourism describes public cultural celebrations around Kanakakunnu Palace and other city venues. Select performances from the current programme.

places.name: Kochi / Thrikkakkara
places.detail: Thrikkakkara Vamana Moorthy Temple is a documented centre of Onam observance. Confirm visitor access and ritual arrangements before planning around it.

timeline.detail: The ten-day festival begins. Floral pookalam designs are part of the seasonal celebrations.
Local preparations and cultural activities develop; public shows follow their own published schedules.
The principal celebration brings the Onasadya feast and family gatherings. Attend a household meal only by invitation.

onam.transport: Choose one city as your base and group venues geographically. Ask your accommodation to confirm the return journey after an evening show rather than relying on an assumed late service.
onam.family: A booked sadya meal and a short public performance offer a manageable starting point. Ask about ingredients and serving arrangements before booking for your family.
onam.accessibility: Ask the venue about seating, toilets, rain cover and a step-free route. For a sadya, confirm table seating if sitting on the floor would be difficult.

suggestedPlan.detail: Choose a public cultural programme and leave an indoor alternative available.
Book a sadya and visit a pookalam display if one is advertised nearby.

tips: Boat races and other local events have separate dates; do not assume they coincide with Thiruvonam.
Temple entry and photography arrangements need local confirmation.

holi.headline: Mathura and Vrindavan for Braj traditions; choose your setting carefully

places.name: Mathura and Vrindavan
places.detail: These are starting points for Krishna-associated celebrations. Select a named temple or organised event and check its own programme.

places.name: Barsana
places.detail: Lathmar Holi is a distinct local tradition. Treat it as a separate visit with its own date and access arrangements, not an automatic addition to Holi day.

timeline.detail: Braj local celebrations can have separate programmes. Match the place you want to visit to its advertised observance.
The bonfire observance takes place on the eve of Holi. Watch from the space designated by the organisers.
Colour play follows; participation should be consensual. Decide whether you want an organised event or a short observational visit.

holi.transport: Arrange your outward and return journeys before joining celebrations. Ask your host about vehicle access and pickup points; leave time to wash and change before a train or long transfer.
holi.family: Choose a supervised event with clear rules on consent and colour use for a first family visit. Ask about an exit route, toilets and a place to change; do not treat a crowded temple celebration as equivalent.
holi.accessibility: Check crowd density, surfaces, colour-free areas and access to washing facilities. Ask whether there is a seated viewing option if you prefer to observe.

suggestedPlan.detail: If appropriate for your group, observe a locally confirmed Holika Dahan.
Attend one agreed celebration, then return for a wash, a meal and rest.

tips: Ask before applying colour; respect anyone who declines.
Keep phones and important belongings in a closed protective pouch.

sources.label: Incredible India · Mathura and Braj traditions

diwali.headline: Choose a city for its local celebration, not a single national programme

places.name: Jaipur
places.detail: Johri Bazar is among the locations highlighted by Incredible India. Plan a compact market and lights walk, checking access locally.

places.name: Ayodhya
places.detail: Deepotsav is a specific public celebration with its own programme and access controls. Confirm its date separately from the Diwali holiday.

places.name: Varanasi
places.detail: Diwali and Dev Deepawali are different observances. Check which one you intend to experience before booking travel.

timeline.detail: Markets and preparations lead into the festival; customs vary between communities.
Lamps, worship and shared celebrations form the focus. Household ceremonies are private unless you are invited.
Regional and family observances continue. Check local arrangements rather than applying one five-day timetable everywhere.

diwali.transport: Choose accommodation within a manageable journey of your chosen lights or market area. Confirm evening transport and road restrictions; arrange a return meeting point before setting out.
diwali.family: Plan a short lights walk with an early return option. Ask your host about noise and quieter indoor spaces if children are sensitive to fireworks.
diwali.accessibility: Check whether the route has steps, barriers or long standing periods. Ask about seating and a quiet alternative; an illuminated street is not necessarily a controlled-access visitor venue.

suggestedPlan.detail: Explore a market and ask locally about the evening route.
Choose one lights walk or a confirmed public event, leaving time for dinner and the return journey.

tips: Do not assume Deepotsav, Diwali and Dev Deepawali share a date.
Check the organiser directly for event access; avoid buying an unspecified promise of priority entry.

sources.label: Incredible India · Diwali and regional examples
Uttar Pradesh Tourism via Incredible India · Ayodhya Deepotsav

pongal.headline: Tamil Nadu: look for an invited community celebration

places.name: Madurai
places.detail: Use Madurai as a base for a locally arranged cultural visit. Ask your host for a named public celebration rather than assuming household rituals are open to tourists.

places.name: Tamil Nadu communities
places.detail: Pongal is a harvest celebration across the state. A confirmed community cooking event can offer a more focused introduction than travelling between cities.

timeline.detail: The opening day begins the four-day sequence.
The Sun is honoured and newly harvested rice is cooked as part of the celebration.
Cattle are honoured; local practices and public events vary.
The fourth day completes the sequence. Confirm the local gathering or outing you plan to attend.

pongal.transport: Arrange travel around the specific host or public event, not an assumed statewide show. For a rural visit, agree the return pickup and exact meeting place in advance.
pongal.family: A hosted cooking demonstration or community meal is a practical family starting point. Bull-related events need a separate decision and confirmed spectator arrangements; they are not necessary to experience Pongal.
pongal.accessibility: Ask about surfaces, toilets, shaded seating and the distance from the vehicle drop-off, especially for a rural or outdoor gathering. Confirm whether you can observe without prolonged standing.

suggestedPlan.detail: Meet your host or visit an advertised public programme and learn about the harvest traditions.
Join an agreed cooking or food experience; leave time for a separate city visit.

tips: Do not enter farms or homes without an invitation.
Keep cooking areas clear and ask before touching decorated animals or ritual objects.

sources.label: Ministry of Tourism · Four-day Pongal sequence

ganesh-chaturthi.headline: Mumbai: choose a small group of mandals

places.name: Lalbaug and Ganesh Galli, Mumbai
places.detail: Incredible India identifies these community celebrations as visitor starting points. Select one rather than assuming several large mandals can fit into a short outing.

places.name: Wadala, Mumbai
places.detail: Another documented area for Ganesh celebrations. Confirm the specific mandal, queue arrangements and visitor entry before travelling.

timeline.detail: Ganesha idols are installed in homes and community pandals.
Aarti, offerings and community activities continue. Households and mandals may keep different observance lengths.
Processions accompany the farewell. Some take place earlier; Anant Chaturdashi marks the major closing observance. Confirm the chosen mandal’s schedule.

ganesh-chaturthi.transport: Check rail or Metro options for the main journey, then confirm walking access to the mandal. On procession days, agree a pickup outside the affected area rather than expecting door-to-door vehicle access.
ganesh-chaturthi.family: Choose a short pandal visit with a clear exit plan. Ask about queue lengths before bringing children, and consider an earlier visit instead of an immersion procession.
ganesh-chaturthi.accessibility: Ask about step-free entrances, seating, queue assistance and accessible toilets. Check whether a special entrance exists before arrival; do not assume priority access is available.

suggestedPlan.detail: Visit one mandal, leaving time for the queue and a food stop.
Choose another local celebration or a permitted viewing area after checking the current programme.

tips: Ask before taking photographs during aarti.
Watch immersions from designated public areas and keep clear of working procession routes.

sources.label: Maharashtra Tourism via Incredible India · Ganesh Chaturthi

navratri.headline: Ahmedabad or Vadodara: choose a garba setting that suits you

places.name: Ahmedabad
places.detail: Gujarat Tourism highlights the city for Navratri. Compare a named public programme with a community garba, checking admission and participation rules.

places.name: Vadodara
places.detail: A strong starting point for varied garba traditions. Decide whether you want to dance, watch, or try a shorter introductory visit.

timeline.detail: Worship and the first gatherings begin the nine-night celebration.
Garba and devotional gatherings continue. Music, format and entry arrangements differ by venue.
Navratri concludes before the tenth-day Dussehra observance. Confirm which programme your ticket or invitation covers.

navratri.transport: Choose one venue per evening and arrange the return journey before dancing. Check the actual finish time and last transport service rather than assuming every event ends at the same hour.
navratri.family: For children or first-time visitors, ask about a spectator area and choose a short early session. Confirm age restrictions and whether re-entry is permitted.
navratri.accessibility: Ask whether the dance surface is level and whether seating, toilets and an accessible entrance are provided. Watching from a seated area can be an alternative to joining the circle.

suggestedPlan.detail: Observe the rhythm and learn the venue’s participation rules.
Return to a setting you enjoyed or try a different community programme by arrangement.

tips: Learn the direction and step pattern before joining a moving circle.
Check dress, footwear and bag rules with the organiser; avoid assuming every venue has the same requirements.

sources.label: Vadodara Municipal Corporation · Local garba traditions

mysuru-dasara.headline: Mysuru: separate palace evenings from procession day

places.name: Mysuru Palace area
places.detail: Palace illumination and cultural programmes provide one way to experience Dasara. Confirm the current hours and public access.

places.name: Jamboo Savari
places.detail: The closing procession is a distinct event. Choose a permitted viewing area and verify entry arrangements separately from ordinary palace admission.

timeline.detail: Ceremonies at Chamundi Hill form part of the festival’s spiritual beginning.
Illumination and cultural performances take place around the city; consult the current programme for each venue.
Jamboo Savari brings the procession through Mysuru. Do not reuse a previous year’s route timings or ticket details.

mysuru-dasara.transport: Build extra time into journeys between venues and check procession-day traffic notices. Agree where a vehicle can collect you after the event rather than relying on the nearest road remaining open.
mysuru-dasara.family: A palace illumination outing or a shorter cultural show can be easier to plan with children than a full procession day. Confirm seating and toilet access before choosing a viewing area.
mysuru-dasara.accessibility: Ask about steps, seating, accessible toilets and the walking distance from the permitted drop-off. Separate palace accessibility information from arrangements for temporary festival enclosures.

suggestedPlan.detail: Explore the city and attend a confirmed evening programme.
Choose another cultural event or, if it is the correct day, plan around the procession with generous time for entry and departure.

tips: Use the organiser’s current ticket information; a palace ticket may not cover a special festival event.
Keep a less crowded alternative in your plan if a viewing area becomes unsuitable.

hornbill-festival.headline: Kisama for the festival; Kohima as a possible base

places.name: Kisama Heritage Village
places.detail: The main cultural setting brings together Naga communities, heritage structures and performances. Choose activities from the current day’s programme.

places.name: Kohima
places.detail: Consider a city base if it suits your accommodation and transport plans. A side trip should leave enough time for the journey to and from Kisama.

timeline.detail: Check the published opening arrangements before planning around a ceremony.
Cultural performances and community presentations provide the core experience. Different days can feature different activities.
Music or events at other venues may have separate schedules and tickets. Confirm their location rather than assuming everything happens at Kisama.

hornbill-festival.transport: Agree the Kohima–Kisama transfer and return pickup in advance. Ask your driver or host about current travel conditions and allow a buffer before an onward journey. Check official visitor entry requirements for your circumstances separately.
hornbill-festival.family: Choose a daytime cultural session, with breaks between performances. Ask food vendors about ingredients, spice levels and serving options rather than assuming every dish suits the group.
hornbill-festival.accessibility: Ask about gradients, steps, surfaces, seating and accessible toilets across the areas you intend to visit. Confirm the drop-off distance and an alternative viewing position if needed.

suggestedPlan.detail: Visit the heritage areas and watch selected performances at an unhurried pace.
Return for a different part of the programme, or allow time for a separate Kohima visit.

tips: Ask before photographing individuals or entering a community structure.
Describe communities by their own names and follow hosts’ instructions around cultural presentations.

pushkar-fair.headline: Pushkar: choose between the fairground and pilgrimage experience

places.name: Fairground
places.detail: Livestock activity and cultural entertainment are different parts of the fair. Ask which will be taking place on your chosen days.

places.name: Pushkar town and lake
places.detail: Religious observance around Kartik Purnima is another focus. Plan town and lake visits separately from fairground activities.

timeline.detail: Trading can follow a different pattern from the advertised cultural programme. Confirm locally if this is the main reason for your visit.
Performances, competitions and fair activities depend on the published schedule.
Pilgrimage and religious observance form part of the fair’s context. Respect worship and avoid blocking access around the lake.

pushkar-fair.transport: Arrange the onward connection to Pushkar and check the permitted drop-off for your accommodation. Within town, plan short walking sections and confirm a return pickup outside any restricted area.
pushkar-fair.family: Choose a short fairground visit and a separate town outing, with water, shade and meal stops planned. Keep children away from animal handling areas and moving livestock.
pushkar-fair.accessibility: Ask about uneven ground, steps near the lake, toilets and seating. Confirm whether your chosen activity can be reached without crossing sand or long unpaved sections.

suggestedPlan.detail: Explore town and choose a cultural activity from the current programme.
Visit the fairground when your preferred activity is confirmed; leave time for the onward journey.

tips: Ask before photographing traders, pilgrims or rituals.
Confirm the full price before agreeing to an activity or guided service.

sources.label: Incredible India · Fair and pilgrimage context
